title: Assistant Accountant - salary negotiable; well-established independent firm
description:
Reed Practice is delighted to be partnering with a highly respected and long-established firm of Chartered Accountants with an excellent reputation across the region.

For almost 60 years, from their office which is commutable easily from Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire, the firm has built strong and lasting relationships with a diverse client base ranging from local businesses to national and international organisations. Due to continued growth and an expanding client portfolio, they are now looking to recruit an experienced Accountant to join their friendly and supportive team.

This is an excellent opportunity for a practice-based professional seeking a varied role within a stable and successful firm that genuinely values its people.

The Role

As Assistant Accountant, you will play a key role in supporting a portfolio of clients, with responsibilities including:
- Support year-end accounts and ensuring client records are accurate and complete.
- Assisting with the preparation of management accounts.
- Processing sales and purchase invoices, receipts, payments and journals.
- Completing bank, credit card and control account reconciliations.
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns accurately and on time.
- Maintaining client records using cloud-based accounting software.
- Liaising directly with clients to resolve bookkeeping queries and obtain financial information.
- Processing payroll and pension submissions (desirable but not essential).

About You

We invite those with the following experience to apply
- AAT qualification or be qualified by experience.
- Previous experience working within an accountancy practice (essential).
- Alternatively, experience managing bookkeeping for multiple entities within a finance environment.
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- A proactive and client-focused approach.

What's on Offer?
- Salary to reflect your experience and calibre - apply to enquire
- Join a well-established and highly regarded accountancy practice.
- Friendly, supportive and collaborative working environment.
- Varied role with exposure to a broad client portfolio.
- Long-term career stability and development opportunities.

To find out more, please contact Natalie Harden at Reed for a confidential discussion, or apply online today for immediate consideration.

title: Underwriting Support Administrator
description:
Underwriting Support Administrator

Our client, a well-established financial mutual, is seeking a Underwriting Support Administratorto join their Operations team, reporting to the Operations Director. The role is responsible for collecting and processing medical and lifestyle information to generate one-off premiums for client care plans, preparing and sending quotes to Financial Advisers, processing applications, and providing ongoing administrative support for active plans.

This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-focused administrator from an insurance, financial services or care background who is confident handling sensitive information and enjoys varied, relationship-led work across advisers, clients and their families.

Key Responsibilities:
- Gather and verify medical, lifestyle and personal information to calculate one-off care plan premiums
- Input data into underwriting and premium calculation tools to generate accurate quotes
- Send quotes to Financial Advisers and respond promptly to queries
- Review completed acceptances for accuracy, following up on any outstanding information
- Maintain accurate records for active plans, including amendments, updates and annual existence checks
- Process death notifications sensitively, verifying documentation and updating records and payments accordingly
- Liaise with family representatives, care providers, Financial Advisers and internal teams
- Work closely with finance to ensure accurate billing, payments and record management
- Act as the main administrative point of contact for Financial Advisers, clients and their families

Requirements
- Strong administrative experience within insurance, financial services or a care setting
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail
- Confident written and verbal communicator, able to convey information clearly to a range of audiences
- Comfortable handling sensitive medical and financial information confidentially
- Understanding of data protection and compliance requirements
- Proficient with IT systems and Microsoft Office
- Experience in underwriting administration or insurance quoting, or knowledge of care plans, is desirable

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a supportive, fully remote team, working across a varied and genuinely meaningful role that supports members and their families at important moments.

title: Part Time Credit Controller
description:
Part-Time Credit Controller & Administrator - 2 Vacancies

Location: Dunstable

Hours: Part-time - flexible working patterns available

Working pattern: Predominantly office based

We are recruiting for two part-time Credit Control / Accounts Administration professionals to join an established and successful business based in the Dunstable area.

These vacancies have arisen due to the planned retirement of two long-standing members of the team, and there is genuine flexibility around both the working hours and how the responsibilities are divided between the two successful candidates.

The business is therefore happy to consider experienced Credit Controllers, Accounts Assistants or strong Finance / Sales Office Administrators with credit control experience.

Depending on experience, responsibilities could include:
- Credit control and management of outstanding customer accounts
- Proactively contacting customers by telephone and email regarding payment
- Resolving invoice and account queries
- Maintaining accurate customer account information
- Supporting accounts payable and wider finance administration
- Processing orders and returns
- Liaising with the warehouse and other internal departments
- General sales office and administrative support

About you

Previous Credit Control experience is essential, although the business is open to candidates with broader accounts or sales administration experience who are comfortable supporting credit control for one of the roles.

Personality is particularly important.

You will need to be confident and comfortable picking up the phone and speaking with customers. You should be personable and able to build strong working relationships, while also being sufficiently assertive and persistent when outstanding payments need to be chased.

Experience using Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central would be particularly advantageous. Alternatively, experience with Sage or another finance, ERP or stock-management system would be welcomed.

Hours & Salary

There is genuine flexibility around how these two part-time positions are structured.

The business is open to discussing different working patterns, including mornings, afternoons, school-friendly hours and four or five-day arrangements, depending on the experience and availability of the successful candidates.

The priority is finding two strong people who can collectively provide good coverage across the working week.

Salary is depending on experience, agreed hours and the balance of responsibilities. There is flexibility to accommodate both a stronger Credit Control profile and someone with broader accounts/administration experience.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking for a stable, long-term part-time position with an established local employer.

Apply now for further information and a confidential discussion regarding the available hours and working patterns.

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Customer Service Advisor

Reports to: Branch Manager / Area Operations Manager
Location: Bedford
Department: Customer Service / Operations

Join Our Team

Our Client is looking for an experienced customer Service Advisor to join their growing team. If you're passionate about delivering exceptional customer service, enjoy building strong customer relationships, and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we'd love to hear from you.

As part of our ambitious growth strategy, our goal is to triple the number of repeat customers over the next five years. This role is central to achieving that ambition by ensuring every customer receives outstanding service, expert support, and a seamless experience from enquiry through to order fulfilment.

The Role

As a Customer Service Advisor, you'll be the first point of contact for many of our customers, providing a friendly, professional, and efficient service across a broad range of products. You'll process customer orders, manage enquiries, resolve issues, and work closely with colleagues across the business to deliver an outstanding customer experience.

This is a varied role that combines customer service, sales support, administration, and operational collaboration, making it ideal for someone who enjoys taking ownership and making a real difference.

What You'll Be Doing
- Deliver outstanding customer service across phone, email, and other communication channels.
- Process customer orders accurately and efficiently, ensuring prompt fulfilment.
- Handle customer enquiries and provide product guidance and recommendations.
- Escalate technical product enquiries to specialist teams where appropriate.
- Resolve customer issues and complaints professionally, achieving positive outcomes.
- Liaise with internal departments and external stakeholders to ensure smooth order processing.
- Follow up quotations and proactively engage with customers.
- Identify and communicate sales opportunities to the External Sales Team.
- Support branch operations, including warehouse or trade counter activities when required.
- Participate in stock cycle counting.
- Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance customer experience and operational efficiency.
- Support the wider branch team and undertake additional duties as required.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who enjoys helping customers, takes pride in delivering excellent service, and works well as part of a team.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience in a customer service, sales support, or internal sales role.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Strong organisational skills with great attention to detail.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities in a busy environment.
- A proactive approach to problem solving and customer service.
- Experience using ERP or order processing systems (desirable).
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
- A willingness to develop product knowledge and learn about our industry.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you'll help ensure:
- Customers receive consistently outstanding service.
- Orders are processed accurately and efficiently.
- Customer enquiries and complaints are resolved quickly and professionally.
- Strong customer relationships are developed and maintained.
- Sales opportunities are identified and passed to the relevant teams.
- The branch achieves improvements in customer retention, sales growth, and operational performance.
- You make a positive contribution to our team culture and business success.

You'll become part of a supportive team where your contribution is recognised, your ideas are valued, and you'll have opportunities to develop your skills and progress your career. Every day brings new challenges, and you'll play an important role in helping us achieve our ambitious growth plans while delivering an exceptional experience for our customers.

Ready to join us?

Apply today and become part of a business that's committed to putting customers first and building lasting relationships.

Please note that at times due to the volume of applications we may not be able to respond to each person individually. If you do not hear from us within 7 days we're sorry you have not been successful this time. Please do not let this stop you applying for other positions you may be suitable for. Good Luck!

title: Partnership Coordinator
description:
Role Overview

The Programme Coordinator will report directly to Strategic Partnership Lead. In this role, you will be responsible for:

Key Responsibilities:

Processes & Documentation:
- Update and maintain delivery plan timelines and milestones.
- Ensure compliance and proper record keeping of Data Sharing Agreements across departments.
- Coordinate with Finance and other teams to manage purchase orders and payments to suppliers.
- Assist in risk management and documentation in collaboration with the Strategic Partnership Lead.

Partner Meetings & Inductions:
- Organise and document minutes and follow-up actions for both internal and external meetings.
- Prepare presentation materials and manage the scheduling and administration and delivery of partner induction sessions.
- Serve as the first point of contact for potential and existing partners, ensuring top-notch service delivery.

Stakeholder Records, Materials, and Information:

- Support the relationship management team by processing and tracking new partner commitments.

Monitoring and Reporting:

- Monitor, analyse, and report on partner engagement, including KPIs and target achievements.

- Proven experience in supporting projects or programmes, particularly in maintaining timelines and project documentation.

- Skilled in supporting meetings, including booking, liaising with stakeholders, and preparing necessary documentation.
- Ability to produce detailed monthly, quarterly, and ad-hoc project status reports.
- Experienced in using databases to monitor or track stakeholder engagement.

Flexible Working

title: Shipping & Logistics Coordinator
description:
Shipping & Logistics Coordinator

Location: Luton
Working Pattern: Fully office-based
Contract: Temporary - With opportunity to go permanent
Start Date: Immediate / ASAP
Hours: 8:30am - 5pm
Rate: £15 per hour

We are currently looking for a Shipping & Logistics Coordinator to join our team in Luton. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced shipping or logistics professional to join a fast-paced manufacturing environment and play a key role in ensuring customer orders are shipped accurately and on time.

Please note: this is a fully office-based position in Luton, with no working from home option.

The Role

As Shipping & Logistics Coordinator, you will be responsible for coordinating customer shipments, working closely with customers, freight forwarders, Planning, Operations and internal support teams to ensure the smooth and timely movement of goods.

Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate customer shipments, including EXW collections.
- Act as the main point of contact for customers regarding shipping arrangements.
- Liaise with freight forwarders and obtain competitive freight quotations.
- Work closely with Planning and Operations to ensure customer orders are shipped on time.
- Prepare shipping and export documentation, including:
- Certificates of Origin
- ATRs
- Commercial invoices
- Certificates of Conformance
- Test certificates
- Support import/export and customs documentation, including SAD documentation.
- Process customer shipments through relevant shipping portals.
- Liaise with the Credit team regarding Letters of Credit.
- Participate in Health & Safety and continuous improvement activities.
- Ensure shipping activities are completed accurately and in line with company procedures and customer requirements.

About You

We are looking for a hands-on, organised and customer-focused individual who is comfortable working in a busy manufacturing environment.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience in shipping, logistics, exports or a similar role.
- Good knowledge of EXW and international shipping processes.
- Experience working with freight forwarders and preparing export documentation.
- Strong communication and organisational skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel.
- Previous SAP experience would be desirable, although full SAP training can be provided.

What We're Looking For

The successful candidate will be someone who can hit the ground running, communicate confidently with customers and internal teams, and ensure shipments are coordinated efficiently and accurately.

If you have experience in shipping or logistics and are available to take on a temporary role in Luton, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Ward Clerk
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for two Ward Clerks at Bedford Hospital, working as a Float within our Ward Clerk team. You will have interaction with patients and relatives as well as staff based at Bedford Hospital. You will be an organised, efficient and motivated individual who is trustworthy and reliable. You must be able to be adaptable within your work role to support the team in all aspects of ward administrative cover.This is an exciting team that will give you the opportunity to grow and develop. The team consists of ward clerks and receptionists that work together sharing their knowledge and experience. Although we have a very strong learning and development function, we appreciate you will need to have acquired some skills and experience from your career in order for your time with us to be a real success. These can be found in the Person and Job Description attachment on NHS Jobs. However we have highlighted some of them below. Educated to GSCE standard or equivalent Experience of working in a customer facing/reception role Experience of using IT package An exciting opportunity has arisen for a ward clerk at Bedford Hospital. To provide both a front line clerical service to clinical staff within the ward whilst also providing "front door" style support to patients and relatives during visits. The post holder will also be responsible for ensuring accurate and timely inputting of patient level data into the relevant clinical systems for the capturing of admission, discharge and transfer of patients. This is to be done whilst also strictly adhering to trust data quality, health records and information governance policies. It is expected that the post-holder will manage their workload in an effective and efficient way and have a flexible approach to covering various wards and the role as it continues to develop with the ever changing needs of the business. The Ward Clerk provides essential administrative and communication support within the ward, acting as a key point of contact for Trust staff, patients and relatives. The post holder will help facilitate effective communication and contribute to the smooth day-to-day running of the ward, ensuring a professional and responsive service at all times. The role is responsible for maintaining accurate records of all patient admissions and discharges, including Hospital Numbers, follow-up appointments, movement of notes and other patient information. The post holder will also update and maintain patient information on Trust IT systems, ensuring all admission, discharge and patient records are accurate and up to date. Duties include, but are not limited to: To update IT systems, including: Admissions Discharges Updating patient details, including correct address, GP details, and next of kin information. To ensure that patients are admitted under the correct Consultant. To file admission packs for new patients in accordance with admission pack filing procedures. To ensure ward trolleys are prepared and ready for Ward Rounds, including ensuring continuation sheets and labels are available for all inpatients. To make follow-up appointments for discharged patients. To file discharge episodes in accordance with discharge filing procedures. In the case of deceased patients, to ensure the correct paperwork is printed for the Bereavement Office and that the GP is contacted. To continually monitor IT systems throughout the working day for any changes in patient status. To support Ward staff in dealing with telephone enquiries. To sort and distribute mail, including re-addressing mail for discharged patients. To report any faults, required repairs, or faulty equipment to the Facilities Help Desk and Clinical Engineering Department. To order non-stock equipment and stationery from Lyreco/ADB, maintaining minimal stock levels in line with next-day delivery availability. To induct and train new members of staff. To carry out any reasonable requests made by the Discharge Officer and Ward staff. The post holder will be expected to undertake all duties in a professional manner, contributing to the effective day-to-day running of the ward and supporting the delivery of high-quality patient care.
